hints: A teleporter may be used only once across all days.
Give each directed edge capacity one and cost one.
Find k units of minimum-cost flow, then decompose the final flow into k routes.
analogy: Each day sends one unit through a network where each teleporter is a single-use ticket.
example: With routes 1->2->4 and 1->3->4, two days cost four teleporters in total.
algorithm: Build a unit-capacity, unit-cost residual network and send k units of minimum-cost flow from 1 to n with shortest augmenting paths and potentials. If fewer than k units are possible print -1. Otherwise follow positive flow edges from source to sink repeatedly, removing each recovered path, and print its vertices and the total cost.
correctness: Integral flow decomposes into source-to-sink paths and cycles; an optimal positive-cost solution contains no flow cycle. Unit capacities make the paths edge-disjoint, and min-cost flow minimizes their total edge count.
complexity: For n rooms, m teleporters and k days, O(k*m log n) time and O(n+m) space, plus output.
